verdict.tagline: Slick digital card combat bogged down by oppressive matchmaking and endless turns.
for_you_if: you want to build competitive decks without spending real money
you enjoy deep trading card game mechanics
not_for_you_if: you expect fair matchmaking as a newcomer
you need reliable account transfer systems
you dislike waiting through lengthy opponent turns

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game offers very little guidance for players wanting to build their own decks from scratch.

citations.review_text:
I’ve come to a clear conclusion: it’s genuinely enjoyable. That said, I’m also a fan of the series and have experience playing the physical card game, which likely enhanced my appreciation for it.

One thing I quickly realized is that the game requires a great deal of strategy. There are plenty of deck archetypes to choose from, but the game offers very little guidance for players who want to build their own decks. A helpful addition would be an optional deck-building assistant that recommends or automatically creates a deck based on the cards a player owns. This would make the experience much more accessible for newcomers while still allowing experienced players to fine-tune their own builds.

Overall, it’s a fun and rewarding game. Once you understand the mechanics and know what you’re doing, the gameplay becomes very engaging, and opening booster packs is especially satisfying.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's performance, noting that it runs smoothly, loads quickly, and is well optimized on PC.

citations.review_text:
(2k+ hours on Master Duel between mobile and PS5; 1k on Duel Links) 

Let alone the direction the franchise itself has chosen (a gameplay where you do 20+ moves first turn to stop your opponent to play, there is no duel, just 1st turn victory/loss)

Let alone the new cards and archetype that are being released that are more and more broken with each new exit (1 card, that has 3 effects and alone moves the duel)

I love Yugioh since I was a child, I'd let ALL OF IT slide, if it wasn't for the bugs ! Cards activation that should activate and instead don't (no, it's not me that doesn't know how effects works in this game, i know my stuff). If you want to report it you have to waste 1h of your life on the KONAMI page, and after 1 year you see it in the patch notes that they fixed it (maybe). I understand that they might get flooded by the average or newest players's reports that doesn't know how excactly thing works, but this is no solution.

It's a pity because the game is well done, personalization is cute enough too, good soundtrack etc, among the YU-GI-OH games this is one you want to play. You can connect KONAMI account and play from multiple consoles with the same account, so yes it has it's strong points. But it's terrible that it take YEARS to fix card effects and almost the same time to file for report for an error you saw. You may also experience anomalous lag (less on PC than phone or consoles), find bots (that too, less with the time) but that aside the game runs smoothly, playing on PC is the most comfortable

Nostalgic YuGiOh enjoyers are in for a big, ugly surprise with the modern YuGiOh dueling. By the time you get the hang of it all, you'll get mad when you see effects not working properly

P.S. No! I don't want to play MAGIC, I want KONAMI to fix his ****

Gems are both expensive enough and given freely enough that it feels much more balanced than any other free 2 play game in terms of progression, especially when you have a pet deck in mind to aim for The Battle Pass is worth it and accessible via gems. Solo Mode is great for testing your decks. I regularly face quite a wide range of decks, even if half of them are still Branded players. Runs much better on my PC than it does my PS4.

YU-GI-OH MASTER DUEL 
is one of the best digital adaptations of the YU-GI-OH! card game. it has smooth gameplay beautiful summon animation and a massive collection of cards.
performance is excellent as well. the game runs smoothly, loads quickly, and is well optimized even during intense duels.
whether you're a competitive duelist or just returning for nostalgia, this game is absolutely worth trying.

This is more of an inbetween negative and positive review, but I wouldn't generally recommend this game. Mechanically, Yugioh is one of the most in-depth and mechanically interesting card games out there. There's many cool themes, play styles, etc. But the game does have the problem of having become chains of overly complicated combos which ultimately lead to the game becoming a case of playing solitare and then letting someone else do the same. It's tedious, and unlikely to change since one of the most popular card archetypes (basically the equivalent of color choices or play styles) is Branded, which has you playing combos for 15 minutes or more and then sitting around waiting for your opponent to do the same. The game's card economy is like most games of this time, horrifically exploitive. But I won't lie, if you do get past all of that, you do find a very rich and engaging game with interesting art and gameplay. IF you do decide to play, make sure to do your research and look up guides on how best to make the most of the game's free currency first. This is a game that doesn't reward, but unfortunately does demand, a lot of patience.

[h3]Title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel[/h3]

Summary: Turn based card game

Personal notes: Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel is the full modern adaptation of the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG. I played a lot of Yu-Gi-Oh! as a kid, loved the show and played a good amount of Duel Links. As such I decided to test Master Duel out as I was told it was more in-depth and true to the series/original card game. I feel like Master Duel offers a much more complete and unrestricted version of Yu-Gi-Oh. In comparision to a game like Duel Links, which is more streamlined and accessible, Master Duel focuses on depth, complexity, and competitive accuracy. The gameplay is standard for TCG's but the deck variety is undeniably deep. There are countless archetypes, combo lines, and interactions to play with, and the game heavily rewards this. When matches are even & going back and fourth, there is a lot of satisfaction in executing a well-built strategy or breaking through a strong opponent. On paper, it offers one of the most complete digital card game experiences available. However, in practice, the design often works against itself. Many duels involve long combo-heavy turns where one player executes 5-10min sequences while the other waits for their response window. While this is part of modern Yu-Gi-Oh!, it can make online matches feel slow and sometimes detached from any active decision-making. The playerbase is also very competitive which leads to a very meta-heavy scene. These decks are crazy strong and while they do showcase depth, I feel like it ruins any sense of variety. I grew up watching and playing Yu-gi-oh with friends and I love the franchise.
And I can say with confidence that this is the most definitive, high-quality online Yu-gi-oh game there has been to date, but it has big problems.

Konami decided to allow only one account per steam account. So if you misread the meta or pulled your favorite cards then found out they weren't viable in the meta anymore, you gotta create a whole new steam account, which is what happened to me.

The Yu-gi-oh TCG itself has a large problem. They have been pumping cards for 25 years now and it is understandable that cards will eventually be powercrept, but most games in the modern meta are resolved within the first turn of the game, which means if the RNG isn't with you on the first draw (no mulligan in Yu-gi-oh), it might save you time to just move onto the next game than wait and watch your opponent set up his board and OTK you in the next 5 minutes.

Added is the fact that, you don't get free packs or gems often to buy in-game booster pack, the meta usually changes every time a new archetype is released, and cards get banned or a number limit pretty easily, that it becomes apparent that it is almost impossible to keep up with meta without spending any money.

I know most people who still play master duel are very sensitive of any criticism towards it, but the game is inching closer and clsoer to an unplayable state, where returning all opponents hands to deck or the potential to dish out 8000 HP worth of burn the first turn is already possible and normalized, because "it's hard to replicate every game".

This is more of a criticism of the card game itself rather than Master Duel. This has been said a million times before and they refuse to address the fundamental flaw of the rules, a turn should not take 10 minutes to complete, nor should you be allowed to combo half the deck in a single turn completely locking out the player that isn't running the latest bullsh*t cards with protection, field wipes, negates, in one giant beater monster. I applaud the attempt at master rule 4 pre 2020 to limit extra deck summoning, but these chicken sh*t heads at Konami reversed it and now the OG fans of the card game are stuck watching these dorks play solitare, before you even get a chance to draw one card(even when you do draw that card, they're going to plays some dumb sh*t hand trap that kick starts another 10 minute combo ON YOUR TURN). Stupid game, there needs to be a solo or casual mode that allows you to earn points to build decks, I refuse to play with these mouth breathers that stink up local tournaments in ranked, I'm surrendering the minute their turn passes 15 seconds.
If you like Old Yugioh this aint it. If you try to play anything its all the new cards and your opponent is playing solitare. Like add a mode to limit card years or something like is that a big ask?

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks permanent alternative game modes, with ranked play being the primary option.

citations.review_text:
I went back and forth on whether to recommend this game or not, but ultimately I do recommend it.

Pros:
 * It's free-to-play, genuinely.
 * It's Yu-Gi-Oh! online, officially.
 * It's the smoothest, most beautiful and consistent simulator.
 * Great crafting system. 3 unwanted cards = 1 card (of your choice) of the same rarity.

Cons:
 * You need to know what you want or the F2P economy will be tough.
 * Everything gets the UR (rarity) tax.
 * It has been 4.5 years since release and there has been no more permanent modes to play. Ranked or nothing.
 * It's Yu-Gi-Oh! online, officially.

TL;DR: The game is great, but it's not 2004 Yu-Gi-Oh!. Don't expect it to be. Cards will fly from both sides the second a duel starts.

I've played YGO off-and-on over the years. I started at the beginning just collecting cool cards and played YGO with friends, then stopped. I picked it back up in the synchro era and had a blast doing silly things, then stopped. Came back again for the Xyz era and still had fun, then stopped. Many years, and multiple master rules, later I came back with Master Duel's release. That gap completely changed the game. Many people hate the game's general direction and others love it. I struggled with it for quite awhile, but eventually I got on board.

For new, new players I have a hard time recommending MD due to the F2P economy along with Yu-Gi-Oh!'s complex wording and gameplay on newer cards. The solo-mode really does not prepare you to play YGO in the current year, and tries to lure you into purchasing bad cards/archetypes early on. You can't just "try a deck", every new deck will have at least 2 UR cards often played at 3.  If you're completely unfamiliar with the game I would recommend both a friend to guide you, and either "Legacy of the Duelist: Link Evolution" or another online simulator. Start with some 2004 decks and play through the different summoning mechanic eras (maybe skip pendulum, they're not super relevant).

Onto things about the game …

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks any built-in chat system for communicating with opponents or friends.

citations.review_text:
Alright, so Bad News; Good news.

Cons:
- The best of 1 format results in many games which are unsatisfying.
- Master Duel holds your hand a bit too much imo. If you're new to the game, take care to understand *why* and *how* you can do things, and not mindlessly click things that are glowing.
- Building multiple decks can get very expensive very quickly. As such, I recommend starting with some of the built-in Structure Decks, which are much cheaper.
- There is NO built-in chat. If you want to play with friends, you will need another way to talk with them.
- There is no "reset account" button. Just like real life, try to be mindful of what you spend money on!
- IMPORTANT: The File size is misleading! Make sure you have a lot of space in whatever drive you're downloading the game to! There's almost 10 GB of patches since the game's release!

Pros:
- Accessibility: Master Duel provides a very quick and convenient platform to play Yugioh. Especially if you don't have a local OTS. 
- Fundamentals: Master Duel provides very base-level teaching of Yugioh's fundamental rules, and a basic understanding of how to play. HOWEVER: If you are learning to play Yugioh, I do NOT recommend jumping straight into the Ladder for ranked play. Take some time to learn a wide variety of decks and cards in the Solo mode gates, before you play in ranked. It will help you better understand how different cards perform different tasks.
- Economy: Master Duel contains a built-in currency in the form of Gems. While you *can* purchase gems with real money, you don't *need* to. Gems can also be earned by: Completing challenges, Advancing your Duel Pass (You have the basic Duel Pass every season, don't worry), Logging in, Climbing the ranked ladder, Meeting daily goals (Examples including competing in a duel without forfeiting, Playing 3 games in Solo mode, and more), and even watching other people's duels! You're also given a large influx of Gems when you make a new account and explore…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe matches where opponents execute extremely long first-turn combos, leaving the other player waiting for minutes before taking an action.

citations.review_text:
It's kind of crazy how you have to have a masters degree in one turn kills just to win. Not really hating on Master Duel for this but Yu-Gi-Oh has gone so far downhill by ruining the balance of the game in recent years. For a version of online Yu-Gi-Oh gameplay, Master Duel is pretty great. Not as good as the golden age of YGOPRO but a very good format of the game. I would not recommend this game to old Yu-Gi-Oh players though, this game is full of sweats and the gameplay has changed for the worst. If you are willing to endure though, the game is pretty generous with in game currency to create the deck you want. You're basically asking to get punished if you don't run the meta though or some sort of scummy one turn kill deck. The animations and art are beautiful, but who's playing Yu-Gi-Oh for screen effects? Some of the ban list differences between this and the TCG are better and worse. Grateful that I can still use Isolde on this format, otherwise I'd be cooked against the meta. Some of the events make other decks/old decks more viable though so even non OP decks have a shot in some formats but that's not the majority of gameplay. 

All in all, expect to get ragebaited, lose more than you win, wait 10 minutes a turn, and watch the game get worse as time goes on.

Turns are way too long. Not an enjoyable experience just watching someone combo for 3 minutes straight. This is further amplified if you have a deck where you have shorter combos/turns, e.g., 30 second turns. A lot of times, you may end a match that took 10 minutes, but you only "played" for 2-3 minutes because of how long the opponent's combo/turn took.

The crafting system is great though - it's very free-to-play friendly relative to other card games and you can easily make whatever deck you want.

As a diehard fan of the franchise since the "power of chaos" era, i really hate this game because the company isn't trying to revive or remaster the older ones, instead of wasting all of that time trying to create new cards that doesn't make any sense, give us the option to play against different characters from the story, i don't want to sit for 15 minutes waiting for these chinese bots to use half of their deck on turn 1... 

I'm sorry but if you feel the need to make over 9000 freaking cards then i think you got bigger problems to take care of konami, i will burn your HQ! RAHHH
